title: Lamb Saag
subtitle: Slow-cooked lamb in spiced spinach sauce
excerpt: Tender chunks of lamb shoulder cooked low and slow in a rich, spiced spinach sauce. The yoghurt stirred in at the end softens the heat and gives the sauce a silky texture. Serve with rice or flatbread.
sourceNotes: Adapted from classic North Indian saag gosht recipes. The technique of wilting and blending the spinach separately keeps the colour vivid.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely before freezing. Reheat gently on the hob, adding a splash of water if needed.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The curry improves overnight as the spices mellow. Refrigerate and reheat gently.

content.text: Cut the lamb into even 4cm cubes so it cooks at the same rate. Patting the pieces dry helps them brown rather than steam.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a stockpot over high heat. Brown the lamb in two batches. Each piece should be deep golden on all sides. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining ghee and reduce heat to medium. Cook the onions for 12 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric, paprika, and chilli flakes. Stir for 1 minute until the spices smell toasted.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until the sauce darkens and the oil separates at the edges.
Return the lamb to the pot. Add 250ml water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 50 minutes.
While the lamb cooks, wilt the spinach in a dry pan or in the microwave. Squeeze out as much water as you can. Blend roughly with a stick blender or food processor.
Stir the spinach into the curry. Cook uncovered for 10 minutes.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the garam-masala. Let it cool for 2 minutes, then stir in the yoghurt. Taste and adjust salt.

items.symptom: Sauce looks grey instead of green
items.cause: Spinach was overcooked or not squeezed dry
items.fix: Add fresh spinach at the end and stir briefly.

items.symptom: Yoghurt has curdled in the sauce
items.cause: Sauce was too hot when yoghurt was added
items.fix: Cool sauce slightly before adding yoghurt next time.

items.symptom: Lamb is still tough after cooking time
items.cause: Pieces were too large or heat too low
items.fix: Cover and cook 20 more minutes on low heat.
